novel_features.name: Quota cost planner
novel_features.description: Dry-run any command sequence and see projected unit cost vs. your remaining 10K-unit daily budget before pressing enter.
novel_features.rationale: Requires a local ledger of past spend keyed by API key plus a unit-cost map for every endpoint — no API exposes either.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Pick this when you need to know if a planned scrape will fit today's budget. Returns total units, per-endpoint breakdown, and remaining budget.

novel_features.name: Cross-corpus FTS search
novel_features.description: FTS5 search across all synced video metadata, transcripts, and comments in one query — no quota cost.
novel_features.rationale: Joins three local FTS5 indexes the API never exposes together; runs offline after sync.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when an agent needs to find which videos discuss a topic across a synced corpus without burning search.list quota (100 units per call).

novel_features.name: Channel digest with FTS
novel_features.description: For a tracked channel, list new uploads since a timestamp joined with transcript-FTS hits for a keyword set.
novel_features.rationale: SQLite join of videos × transcripts × channels filtered by publishedAt and FTS in a single command — no MCP server does this.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this for weekly newsletter sweeps, agent research loops, or any 'what did this creator say about X this week' question.

novel_features.name: Trending list diff
novel_features.description: Diff today's `mostPopular` snapshot against an earlier date and show entries that entered, exited, or moved.
novel_features.rationale: Powered by the trending_snapshots table the sync workflow populates; the API itself never returns historical trending.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Pick this to detect rising or falling trending entries between two dates — useful for content trend reports and sentiment shifts.

novel_features.name: Per-video velocity
novel_features.description: Compute Δviews, Δlikes, and Δcomments per day per video over a rolling window from your local snapshot history.
novel_features.rationale: Requires successive videos.list snapshots in the local store; the API only returns current totals.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when you need 'which uploads from the last 30 days are accelerating or dying' — a question Studio shows piecemeal but agents can't extract.

novel_features.name: Topic-trending crossover
novel_features.description: Find videos in trending snapshots whose title, description, or transcript mention a keyword, ranked by trending position.
novel_features.rationale: Three-table join of trending_snapshots × videos × transcripts that no API endpoint covers.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use to spot when a niche topic crosses into mainstream trending lists — a signal for editorial timing.

novel_features.name: Subscription feed rebuild
novel_features.description: OAuth-gated: rebuild the subscription feed locally — list subscribed channels' new uploads since a timestamp in chronological order.
novel_features.rationale: Joins subscriptions.list with cached uploads playlists; the YouTube subscription feed itself is not exposed via the API.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Pick this for an agent-readable replacement of the in-app subscription feed: filterable, sortable, replayable.

novel_features.name: Quota ledger audit
novel_features.description: Show the rolling per-API-key ledger of every command's quota spend, aggregated by command, endpoint, and day.
novel_features.rationale: Reads a local quota_log sidecar table populated by every command — no API exposes per-call billing detail.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use after a quota-exceeded surprise to find the offending command, or daily to budget across multiple agents sharing one key.

narrative.headline: Every YouTube Data API v3 endpoint, plus quota-aware planning, plus offline transcripts (no quota), plus an SQLite-backed store so channel and trending analysis cost zero quota after sync.
narrative.value_prop: Existing tools split the surface — yt-dlp owns downloads, MCP servers own metadata reads, no one lets an operator do all three plus track quota plus query a cached corpus. youtube-pp-cli mirrors all 23 Data API resources, shells out to yt-dlp for transcripts, and ships a local SQLite store with FTS5 across video metadata, transcripts, and comments. Use `quota plan` before running expensive sweeps and `corpus search` to query everything you've already synced without touching the API.
narrative.auth_narrative: Read commands need a YouTube Data API key (10K-unit/day quota by default). Set `YOUTUBE_API_KEY` or pass `--api-key`. Write commands (playlist edits, comments, ratings, uploads, channel section CRUD, subscriptions, captions, thumbnails) require OAuth2 — run `youtube-pp-cli auth login` to harvest a token into `~/.config/youtube-pp-cli/oauth.json`. Transcripts use yt-dlp and require neither.

quickstart.comment: Verify YOUTUBE_API_KEY is set, yt-dlp is on PATH, and the API is reachable

quickstart.command: youtube-pp-cli youtube search-list --q 'go generics' --part snippet --type video --max-results 25 --json
quickstart.comment: Search the API directly; JSON-piped to jq or stdout
Mirror a channel's uploads + stats into the local SQLite store
FTS across everything you've synced — zero quota
Preview projected quota cost before running real commands

troubleshoots.fix: Run `youtube-pp-cli cost ledger --last 24h` to find the offending command. Use `--data-source local` on read commands to skip the API entirely after sync.
search.list won't surface videos older than ~6 months or unindexed regions. Try `youtube-pp-cli channels videos <id>` instead — it crawls the uploads playlist directly.
Install yt-dlp via `brew install yt-dlp` (macOS) or `pip install yt-dlp`. The CLI prints an `oauth required` style error when it shells out and yt-dlp is missing.
Run `youtube-pp-cli auth login` to refresh the OAuth token. The token is stored at `~/.config/youtube-pp-cli/oauth.json`.
The video may have no captions. Try `--lang auto` to let yt-dlp pick auto-generated captions, or check `youtube-pp-cli captions list <video>` for available language codes.

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI when an agent or operator needs the full YouTube Data API surface plus offline analysis. It excels at multi-channel research sweeps, quota-aware bulk operations, transcript corpora for retrieval, and time-series questions Studio cannot answer (velocity, trending diffs, topic crossover). Reach for it any time a question requires joining videos, channels, transcripts, comments, or trending lists across time — those are the gaps every other YouTube tool leaves open.

recipes.title: Weekly research sweep with select narrowing
recipes.explanation: Joins last 7 days of uploads against transcript FTS for two keywords, then narrows the deeply-nested response to the four fields an agent actually needs — keeps payload under 4 KB even with 50 hits.

recipes.title: Plan before you scrape
recipes.explanation: Sums the projected unit cost of a search.list (100u) plus a videos.list (1u) against your remaining daily budget so you know if today's run will fit.

recipes.title: Trending diff over a week
recipes.explanation: Compares the latest trending_snapshots row against the snapshot taken on April 1st and emits entered/exited/moved buckets.

recipes.title: Cross-corpus search agent path
recipes.explanation: FTS5 union across videos, transcripts, and comments — `hits.kind` tells the agent whether each match came from metadata, a transcript, or a comment, so it can weight relevance accordingly.

recipes.title: Find rising videos in a channel
recipes.explanation: Compares last 30 days of cached snapshots and ranks the channel's videos by view-velocity (views/day) so you can spot the breakouts.
